notes: $16.00 is the rate outside NYC, Nassau, Suffolk and Westchester ($17.00 there); see cities/ny-new-york.json.
Additional NY meal rules (20 min between 5-7 p.m. for shifts from before 11 a.m. to after 7 p.m.; 45 min for >6 h shifts starting 1 p.m.-6 a.m.) not encoded.
NY spread-of-hours: 1 extra hour at minimum wage when the spread exceeds 10 hours (DOL table); not encoded.
Mercantile establishments must give 24 consecutive hours of rest each week (DOL table).
No state daily overtime listed in the DOL table.
Drafted from US DOL WHD state tables (confidence=medium) on 2026-11-06; upgrade to primary sources pending.

Minors: NY 16-17 school-week 4 h cap applies to days preceding a school day (Sun-Thu, but Sunday is excepted, 8 h); the validator treats Mon-Fri as school days, so Friday is enforced at 4 h (stricter than law).

Minors: 16-17 may work to midnight before a school day only with written parental consent + school academic-standing certificate (and before a non-school day with parental consent); encoded latest_end = 10 p.m.
Minors: extra param key max_days_week (6) for NY; NY 16-17 non-school-week alternative schedule (10 h one day, 9 h four days, max 48 h) not encoded.
Minimum wage from 2027 is CPI-indexed (Lab. Law § 652(1-b)); NYS DOL says the 2027 rate stays $16.00 / $17.00 (off-ramp met): https://dol.ny.gov/minimum-wage-0.

rules.summary: New York requires 1.5x pay after 40 hours in a workweek.

rules.summary: New York requires a 30-minute noonday meal period for shifts over 6 hours that span the noon meal period.

citation.title: US DOL WHD — State meal-period requirements (rev. Jan. 1, 2023)
citation.excerpt: 30 minute noonday period for employees who work shifts of more than 6 hours that extend over the noon day meal period

rules.summary: While school is in session, 14- and 15-year-olds may work at most 3 hours on a school day, 8 on a non-school day, 18 hours and 6 days a week, between 7 a.m. and 7 p.m.

citation.title: N.Y. Lab. Law § 142 — Hours of work for minors 14 and 15
citation.excerpt: When school is in session ... More than three hours on any school day; b. More than eight hours on any day when school is not in session; c. More than eighteen hours a week

rules.summary: When school is not in session, 14- and 15-year-olds may work at most 8 hours a day, 40 hours and 6 days a week, 7 a.m.-7 p.m. (9 p.m. from June 21 to Labor Day).

citation.title: N.Y. Lab. Law § 142 — Hours of work for minors 14 and 15
citation.excerpt: When school is not in session ... a. More than eight hours a day; b. More than six days a week; c. More than forty hours a week

rules.summary: While school is in session, 16- and 17-year-olds may work at most 4 hours on a day before a school day, 8 on Fri/Sat/Sun/holidays, 28 hours and 6 days a week, 6 a.m.-10 p.m. (midnight with parent consent and school certificate).

citation.title: N.Y. Lab. Law § 143 — Hours of work for minors 16 and 17
citation.excerpt: More than four hours on any day preceding a school day, other than on a Sunday or holiday ... More than eight hours on a Friday, Saturday, Sunday or holiday; c. More than twenty-eight hours a week

rules.summary: When school is not in session, 16- and 17-year-olds may work at most 8 hours a day (10 on one day / 9 on four days to make shorter days), 48 hours and 6 days a week, not between midnight and 6 a.m.

citation.title: N.Y. Lab. Law § 143 — Hours of work for minors 16 and 17
citation.excerpt: When school is not in session ... a. More than eight hours a day ... b. More than forty-eight hours a week; c. More than six days a week

rules.summary: New York's minimum wage is $16.00 an hour outside NYC, Nassau, Suffolk and Westchester from January 1, 2026 (unchanged on Jan. 1, 2027 per NYS DOL).

citation.title: N.Y. Lab. Law § 652(1-a)(c) — Minimum wage, remainder of state
citation.excerpt: every employer shall pay ... for each hour worked outside the city of New York and the counties of Nassau, Suffolk, and Westchester ... $16.00 on and after January 1, 2026
